<STRUCT_0001>
Here is a characterization of unramified morphisms in terms of the
diagonal morphism.

Let <MATH_0001> be a morphism.
<STRUCT_0001>
<STRUCT_0002> If <MATH_0002> is unramified, then the diagonal morphism
<MATH_0003> is an open immersion.
<STRUCT_0003> If <MATH_0004> is locally of finite type
and <MATH_0005> is an open immersion, then <MATH_0006> is unramified.
<STRUCT_0004> If <MATH_0007> is locally of finite presentation and <MATH_0008> is an open
immersion, then <MATH_0009> is G-unramified.
<STRUCT_0005>

The first statement follows from
Algebra, Lemma <REF_0001>.
The second statement from the fact that <MATH_0001>
is the conormal sheaf of the diagonal morphism
(Lemma <REF_0002>)
and hence clearly zero if <MATH_0002> is an open immersion.

It also implies (2) because by
Lemma <REF_0002>

This in particular shows that (3), (4) and (5) are equivalent.
The support of <MATH_0016> is closed in <MATH_0017>, see
Modules, Lemma <REF_0005>.
Assumption (3) implies that <MATH_0018> is not in the support.
Hence <MATH_0019> is zero in a neighbourhood of <MATH_0020>, which
implies (1). The equivalence of (1) and (3) applied to <MATH_0021>
implies the equivalence of (2) and (4).
At this point we have seen that (1) -- (5) are equivalent.
